body:
### Describe the bug

Cython 3.0–3.3 incorrectly assumes PyErr_Occurred() is non-NULL in async-generator athrow handling. When an injected exception causes the generator to suspend without setting a new exception, this results in PyExceptionClass_Check(NULL) and a segmentation fault.

Native stack (gdb, Cython 3.2.9):

#0  Py_TYPE(ob)                                   ob == NULL
#1  PyExceptionClass_Check(err)
#2  __Pyx_PyErr_GivenExceptionMatches2(err=NULL, PyExc_StopAsyncIteration, PyExc_GeneratorExit)
#3  __Pyx_async_gen_athrow_throw                  (aclose mode, retval != NULL)

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```cython
class Suspend:
    def __await__(self):
        yield


async def agen():
    try:
        yield 1
    finally:
        for _ in range(3):
            try:
                await Suspend()
            except ValueError:
                pass


g = agen()
try:
    g.__anext__().send(None)
except StopIteration:
    pass
closer = g.aclose()
closer.send(None)           # GeneratorExit goes in, the finally block suspends
closer.throw(ValueError())  # the generator suspends again: segfault
```

### Expected behaviour

The same as CPython: closer.throw(ValueError()) returns None (the value of the next suspension), and the close goes on. Run as plain Python, the code above finishes without error.

Actual behaviour: "Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault".

### OS

Linux x86_64 (GCC 15). The crash is the same at -O0, -O2 -DNDEBUG and -O3 -DNDEBUG.

### Python version

3.13.2 (also seen in production on 3.13.15)

### Cython version

3.0.12, 3.1.6, 3.2.0, 3.2.9, 3.3.0 and master (418acffa8) all crash.

### Additional context

_No response_
title: [BUG] Segfault when throwing into a pending async generator aclose() that suspends again
